title: Google Business Profile Setup Guide for Pakistan
desc: How to claim, verify and fill in a free Google Business Profile so people near you can find, call and visit your business. Steps, rules and common mistakes.
answer: A Google Business Profile is the free listing that shows your business name, phone number, hours, photos and reviews on Google Search and Google Maps. Claim it, verify it, choose your categories carefully, fill in every field honestly, and ask real customers for reviews. Google says you cannot pay for a better local ranking, so completeness and accuracy are your main levers.
body: p

Last verified: 24 November 2026, against Google Business Profile Help pages listed under Sources. Google changes the screens and options often, so the exact buttons may look different when you try this.
h2
What a Google Business Profile is
p

When someone searches for "dentist near me" or "AC repair Lahore", Google often shows a map and a short list of businesses. Each entry comes from a Google Business Profile. It shows your name, address or service area, phone number, opening hours, photos and customer reviews. Google used to call it Google My Business, and many people still search with that old name.
p
The profile is free. You do not need a website to create one, but a website gives people a place to learn more once they find you.
h2
Why it matters for a Pakistani business
p

A lot of customers search on their phone, often when they need something today. A clinic, a salon, a restaurant or an electrician gets chosen quickly, usually from what is visible on the first screen: the rating, the photos and a phone number to tap.
p
If your profile is missing, wrong or unclaimed, you lose that moment. Someone else's profile, or a wrong phone number on an old listing, gets the call instead.
h2
Step 1: Check whether your business already has a listing
p

Search for your business name on Google and in Google Maps. Maps often has a listing already, created from public information or by a customer. If you find it, claim it instead of creating a second one. Google's guidelines say there should be only one profile per business.
h2
Step 2: Create or claim the profile
p

Sign in with a Google account that you control, ideally one that belongs to the business owner and not to an employee or an outside freelancer. If that person leaves, you could lose access. Then search for your business inside Google Business Profile and follow the prompts, or add it as a new business.
h2
Step 3: Use your real business name
p

Google says your name should reflect your real-world name, as used on your signboard and known to customers. It does not allow marketing taglines, phone numbers, hours, service descriptions or location details inside the name.
p

So "Al-Noor Dental Clinic" is fine. "Al-Noor Dental Clinic Best Dentist Lahore Open 24 Hours" is the kind of name that can get your profile suspended or edited. It is tempting to add keywords, but it breaks the rules.
h2
Step 4: Choose your categories
p

Pick one primary category that says what your business is, then add secondary ones only if they are true. Google's wording is that a category should complete the sentence "This business IS a", not "This business HAS a". A restaurant that also has a parking lot does not add "parking lot" as a category.
h2
Step 5: Add your address, or hide it if you travel to customers
p

If customers visit you, add your exact location. Pakistani addresses can be hard to place on a map, so check the pin by zooming in and dragging it to your actual door. Use the address text people recognise, with a nearby landmark in the description if it helps.
p

If you go to customers, for example a plumber, a tutor or a mobile mechanic, Google calls you a service-area business. Google says these businesses should hide their address and list a service area instead. For most businesses that area should not stretch beyond about two hours of driving from where you are based.
h2
Step 6: Verify the profile
p

Verification proves the business is really yours. Google decides which methods you see, and you cannot change that. Depending on your business, region and public information, the options can include a phone or text code, an email, a video call, a video recording or a postcard with a 5-digit code. Postcards usually take around two weeks, and the code expires after 30 days. After you finish, Google reviews your details, which can take up to 5 business days.
p

If a method does not appear for you, that is Google's decision, not a mistake on your side. Try again later or use another method if one is offered, and contact Google Business Profile support if you stay stuck.
h2
Step 7: Fill in everything that is true
p
Google says businesses with complete and accurate information are more likely to show up in local search results. Fill in these fields:
ul
Phone number: use one that someone answers during business hours, written the way people dial it.
Website: link to the page that matches the profile, ideally one with a clear call or WhatsApp button.
Opening hours: set your regular hours, then update special hours for Eid and other holidays so people do not arrive at a closed door.
Services or products: list what you really offer, with short plain descriptions.
Description: say what you do and who you serve in plain words. Google does not allow links, prices or promotions in the description.
Photos: your signboard, the entrance, the inside, your team and real work. A customer who has never visited you wants to know what they will find.
h2
Step 8: Ask for reviews the honest way
p

Reviews are part of what Google calls prominence, one of the three main factors in local results, alongside relevance and distance. Your profile has a link and a QR code that you can share with customers. Send it by WhatsApp after a job is done, or print the QR code at your counter.
p

Do not pay for reviews and do not offer a discount or a free item in exchange for one. Google treats incentivised reviews as fake and misleading content. Do not ask friends who never used your service either. A small number of real reviews is safer than a large number of bought ones.
p
Reply to reviews, including the bad ones. Keep the reply short, polite and specific, and never share a customer's private details.
h2
What a profile cannot do
p

Google states there is no way to request or pay for a better local ranking. A complete profile makes you eligible and easier to choose. It does not guarantee a top position, calls or sales, and results depend on your category, your area, your competitors and how customers rate you.
p

If you want people to find you through paid search as well, a profile and a working [website](/services/website-development/) make that traffic more useful, because visitors can check your reviews and photos before they contact you.
h2
Common mistakes we would check first
ul
Keywords or a phone number stuffed into the business name.
A pin that sits on the wrong street.
Two profiles for the same shop.
The profile owned by a former employee or an agency that no longer works with you.
Old opening hours, especially around Eid.
A website link that goes to a homepage with no obvious way to contact you.
p

faq: Is a Google Business Profile free?
Yes. Creating and managing the profile costs nothing. You only pay if you choose to run Google Ads separately.
Do I need a website to create one?
No. You can create and verify a profile without a website. A website still helps, because people usually want more detail before they contact you.
I work from home and visit customers. Should I show my home address?
Google says service-area businesses should hide their address and list the areas they serve. Follow that rule so your home address is not public.
Can I pay Google to rank higher in the map results?
No. Google states there is no way to request or pay for a better local ranking. Paid ads are separate and appear as ads.
It depends on the method Google gives you. Google says its review can take up to 5 business days, and postcards usually arrive in about two weeks.
